title: Pattern avoidance in canon permutations
summary: A canon permutation is a $k$-regular word over $[n]$ in which, for each $j$, the $j$-th copies of the letters form the same permutation $σ$. These were introduced by Elizalde as a generalization of nonnesting multipermutations, which are the case $k = 2$. We study classical pattern avoidance in them for arbitrary $k$. We show that avoiding any one of $112$, $122$, $211$ or $221$ is counted by the $k$-Catalan numbers $\frac{1}{n}\binom{kn}{n-1}$.
